summary: Dependency-confusion squat with install-time host identifier exfiltration to OAST/webhook.site
details: @capsense/ccx-welcome-page@99.99.99 is published under a private-looking scope at an implausibly high version (99.99.99), a shape designed to win resolution against an internal package of the same name. All three npm lifecycle hooks (preinstall, install, postinstall) in package.json invoke `node beacon.js`, which collects os.hostname(), os.userInfo().username, os.platform(), and the lifecycle stage, encodes them into a DNS label plus query string, and transmits them to a third-party interactsh OAST subdomain (*.oast.pro) via dns.lookup and https.get, and to a webhook.site collector endpoint. The package's own description self-labels as a dependency-confusion proof-of-concept, but the behavior performed on `npm install` is unauthenticated exfiltration of installer host and user identifiers to attacker/third-party-controlled collection infrastructure, and the same lifecycle hooks could deliver arbitrary code to any build system that resolves this public package in place of a private internal one.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
